channel.title: Toyota recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Toyota trucks and SUVs have wrong weight capacity labels
item.description: The sticker inside your door that tells you how much weight your vehicle can safely carry shows the wrong numbers. It was added after the truck or SUV was built to account for extra equipment, and the added-weight figure printed on it is inaccurate. If you trust that label when loading people, cargo, or towing gear, you could put more weight in the vehicle than it was designed to handle.

item.title: Toyota Camry Hybrid dash display failure disables hazard lights
item.description: On certain 2025-2026 Toyota Camry Hybrids, the instrument cluster — the display screen behind the steering wheel — can fail as you start the car. When it fails, the hazard lights, turn signals, seat belt warning, and smart key reminder all stop working. That means other drivers cannot see when you are signaling a turn or warning them of trouble. The vehicles do not meet several federal safety rules. Dealers will update the display software for free.

item.title: Toyota Tacoma shock parts can rust off onto road
item.description: Shock absorbers are the parts that soak up bumps. On these trucks, a metal flange on the front and rear shocks can corrode and break, letting the external oil canister attached to the shock come loose and fall off. A heavy metal part dropping onto the roadway becomes a hazard for your truck and for the drivers behind you. Toyota expects to mail owner notification letters starting September 21, 2026.

item.title: Toyota Land Cruiser Hybrid cluster may hide warning lights
item.description: On certain Toyota Land Cruiser Hybrids and some related Toyota and Lexus models, the display screen in front of the driver may fail to show some warning lights and gauges. That means you might not be told about problems such as engine coolant getting too hot or trouble with the electrical charge, so you could keep driving with a fault you know nothing about. Toyota fixes this with a free software update sent to the car over the air.

item.title: Toyota Tundra engine can fail and lose power
item.description: Some 2024 Toyota Tundra pickups with the V35A engine may have leftover debris from the factory inside the engine. That debris can wear out a main bearing, a part the engine needs to turn smoothly. If the bearing fails, the engine can quit while you are driving and the truck loses power. Dealers will check the bearing using inspection software and driving data, and replace the engine if needed, free of charge.

item.title: Toyota RAV4 front seat brackets may be poorly welded
item.description: Toyota found that some 2025 RAV4 vehicles left the factory with bad welds on the metal brackets that hold the front seats to their rails. Those brackets are what keep your seat anchored to the floor. If the welds are weak, a front seat may not hold you firmly in place during a crash, so you could be thrown around or hit part of the car. Dealers will look at the welds and fix them if needed.

item.title: Toyota Corolla Cross Hybrid backup warning sound too quiet
item.description: Hybrids run so quietly that people nearby may not hear them, so federal rules require them to make a warning sound. On these Corolla Cross Hybrids, the sound the car makes when backing up is not loud enough. Someone walking behind the vehicle may not realize a car is moving toward them. Nothing about how the car drives or stops is affected. A dealer can fix it with a free software update to the warning sound system.

item.title: Toyota and Lexus vehicles carry wrong weight capacity label
item.description: On many recent Toyota and Lexus models, the sticker that tells you how much added weight the vehicle can carry shows incorrect numbers. That label is what owners use to judge how many passengers plus how much luggage, gear or cargo is safe to load. Because the figures are wrong, you could load the vehicle heavier than it is built to handle without realizing it. The dealer replaces the label free.

item.title: Toyota Highlander second-row seat backs may not lock
item.description: On these Highlanders, the second-row seat backs may fail to lock in place after someone adjusts them. That means a seat back that looks set may not actually be latched. In a crash, an unlocked seat back may not hold the person sitting there the way it should, which could lead to injury. Dealers will replace the springs inside the seat back recliner so the seat locks properly. Toyota is handling this recall in stages, so your repair may be scheduled later.

item.title: BMW and Toyota Supra Starter Can Overheat and Catch Fire
item.description: Wear on a part inside the engine's starter motor can make the starter overheat and catch fire. A fire in the engine bay can spread and injure you or your passengers. The repair is straightforward: a dealer replaces the whole starter motor at no charge. Owner letters were mailed July 21, 2026, and the recall covers both the listed BMW models and the Toyota Supra, so check which brand's service line applies to you.

item.title: Toyota Prius rear door may open while driving
item.description: Water can get into the switch inside a rear door and cause a short circuit. If that happens, an unlocked rear door can pop open on its own, including while the car is moving. The dealer will change the wiring for the rear door switches at no cost. This recall replaces an earlier one, so even if your car was already fixed under the older recall, it needs the new repair done.

item.title: Toyota Tundra rearview camera may not show image
item.description: Some 2024-2025 Toyota Tundra and Tundra Hybrid trucks with the Panoramic View Monitor camera system may not show the backup camera picture when you shift into reverse. Without that picture you cannot see a small child, a pet, or an object sitting directly behind the truck while you are backing up. A dealer will update the parking assist software for free. Toyota began mailing owner notification letters in March 2026.

item.title: Rollx Wheelchair Vans: Restraints May Not Lock Wheelchair
item.description: These are vans converted by Rollx for wheelchair use. The straps that hold a wheelchair use retractors, which work like a seat belt: they pull in slack and then lock so the chair cannot roll. On these vans, the QRT-Deluxe and QRT-Max retractors may fail to lock. If they do not lock, the wheelchair and the person in it can shift or slide while the van is moving, which raises the risk of injury. Rollx and the restraint maker will check the retractors and replace them if needed.

item.title: Toyota Highlander third-row center belt anchor misaligned
item.description: On certain 2024-2025 Highlander and Highlander Hybrid models, the anchor that holds the third-row center seat belt to the roof may have been bolted on at the wrong angle. Because it sits crooked, that belt may not hold the person in the middle of the back row properly if the vehicle is hit. Dealers will take the anchor off and reinstall it correctly with a new bolt, free of charge.

item.title: Wheelchair van restraints may not lock in Odyssey, Pacifica, Sienna
item.description: These minivans were converted by Vantage Mobility so a wheelchair can ride inside. The wheelchair is held down by belt-style restraints with retractors that are supposed to lock, much like a seat belt locks. On these vans, the retractors may fail to lock, so the wheelchair is not really tied down. If it is not secured, the chair and the person in it can roll or tip while the van is moving, braking, or turning.

item.title: Toyota Camry Hybrid inverter bolt may cause power loss
item.description: A bolt inside the inverter — the box that sends power from the hybrid battery to the electric motor — may not have been tightened enough on some 2025-2026 Camry Hybrids. With a loose bolt, the connection may not be solid. That can make the car suddenly lose the power that drives the wheels, and it can also cause an electrical short that starts a fire while the car is on. Toyota dealers will replace the whole inverter at no cost.

item.title: Toyota Tundra engine may fail and stall
item.description: Small bits of leftover material from the factory may be inside the engine. That debris can damage the main bearings, which are the parts that let the engine's crankshaft spin smoothly. If a bearing fails, the engine can shut off while you are driving and you lose the ability to accelerate. A dealer will check the number one main bearing using special software and driving data, and if there is a problem, they will replace the entire engine at no cost to you.

item.title: Toyota, Lexus and Subaru Solterra rearview cameras may freeze
item.description: These vehicles have a Panoramic View Monitor system that shows what is behind and around you. A software error can make the backup camera image freeze or go completely blank when you shift into reverse. That means you may not see a child, a pet or an object behind the vehicle. Federal rules require a working rear view. A dealer will update the parking assist software at no cost; it is a software fix, not a part replacement.

item.title: Toyota Sienna Hybrid second-row seat rails welded badly
item.description: The rails that the second-row seats are mounted on may have been welded incorrectly at the factory. A bad weld can let the seat shift or come loose in a crash, so the seat may not hold the person sitting in it the way it should, and that passenger could be hurt worse. Dealers will replace the second-row seat rails free of charge. Toyota is handling this recall in phases, so parts may not be available for every owner right away.

item.title: Toyota Tacoma front driveshaft joint may break
item.description: On these 2025 Toyota Tacomas, a joint in the front driveshaft can deform and then break. If it breaks, steering can become difficult while you are driving. On full-time four-wheel-drive versions, a broken driveshaft can also let the truck roll away while parked if the parking brake is not set. A dealer will inspect both front driveshaft assemblies and replace them if needed, at no cost to you.

item.title: Toyota Tundra and Sequoia Backup Camera May Not Appear
item.description: A software error can keep the backup camera picture from showing up on the center screen when you shift into reverse. Without it, you cannot see children, pets or objects directly behind the truck, and these vehicles no longer meet the federal rear-visibility rule. A dealer will update the multimedia display software free of charge, with no parts involved. Toyota mailed owner letters on November 19, 2025, so you can book the repair now.

item.title: BMW X3, X4 and Z4 starter relay fire risk
item.description: The relay that switches power to the engine's starter can corrode. A corroded relay can overheat and short out, and that can start a fire. This recall also covers the Toyota Supra, which uses the same part. BMW says park outside and away from buildings until the repair is finished. Dealers replace the engine starter at no cost. Owner letters were mailed February 6, 2026, and these VINs became searchable on the NHTSA site in November 2025.

item.title: Toyota and Lexus dashboard may not show speed or warnings
item.description: When these Toyota and Lexus vehicles start up, a software error can leave the instrument panel, the display behind the steering wheel, missing important information. Your speed may not appear, and the warning lights for the brake system and for low tire pressure may not light up. That means you would not know how fast you are going, or that the brakes or tires need attention. Most vehicles get a free software update sent to the car wirelessly.

item.title: Toyota bZ4X and Subaru Solterra defroster can stop working
item.description: If the heating and cooling system in these electric SUVs develops a fault — for example, if the electric compressor fails — the defroster and defogger can stop working. That means you may not be able to clear fog or ice from the windshield, so your view of the road can get much worse in cold or damp weather. Dealers will reprogram the software that runs the climate system and will check the electric compressor, replacing it free if it is bad.

item.title: Toyota Tundra reverse lights can fail from moisture
item.description: Water can get into the housings for your truck's reverse lights — the white lights that come on when you shift into reverse. Moisture inside can make one or both lights stop working. Without them, it's harder for you to see behind you at night, and people walking or driving behind you don't get the usual signal that you're about to back up. Your dealer will replace both reverse light assemblies and fix the wiring if needed, at no cost.

item.title: Toyota Sienna Hybrid third-row seatback bolts may be loose
item.description: On these Sienna Hybrid minivans, the bolts holding the seatbacks of the third-row seats may not have been tightened enough at the factory. A loose seatback may not hold a person in place in a crash, and it also affects the head restraints and the anchors used for child car seats, so the vehicles do not meet federal safety rules. A Toyota dealer will tighten the bolts for free. The repair is just tightening the bolts already in the van, so no new parts are needed.

item.title: Toyota Tacoma rear brake hoses can leak fluid
item.description: On four-wheel-drive Tacomas, mud and dirt can pack up inside the rear wheels and rub against the rear brake hoses. Over time that damages the hoses and brake fluid can leak out. Losing brake fluid means the brakes do not work as well as they should, so the truck may take longer to stop. Dealers will replace both rear brake hoses free of charge.

item.title: Toyota Camry Hybrid rear center seat belt may be damaged
item.description: The seat belt in the middle of the second-row seat may have damaged webbing — the woven strap that holds you in place. Toyota says the belt does not meet the federal safety standard for seat belt assemblies. If that strap is damaged, it may not hold a passenger properly. A dealer will look at the belt and install a whole new seat belt assembly if it is damaged, at no cost. Toyota mailed owner letters on March 20, 2025.

item.title: Toyota and Lexus vehicles may have disabled driver's airbag
item.description: Certain Toyota Corolla, Corolla Cross, Corolla Cross Hybrid, Highlander, Highlander Hybrid and Tacoma vehicles, plus Lexus RX350, NX250 and NX350 models, may have been repaired incorrectly under an earlier recall. Inside the steering column is a coiled ribbon of wiring that carries power to the airbag in the steering wheel. A weld in that connection may not have been done properly, so the connection can come apart and shut the driver's airbag off. The airbag then will not inflate in a crash.

item.title: Toyota Camry and Lexus fuel pumps may stall engine
item.description: The low-pressure fuel pump sits inside the gas tank and sends gasoline to the engine. On certain 2018 Camry, 2019 Lexus NX300 and 2019 RX350L vehicles, that pump can fail. When it does, the engine can stall, which may happen while you are moving — in an intersection, merging, or on the highway. Toyota and Lexus dealers will replace the whole fuel pump assembly for free. Owner letters for this recall were mailed in March 2025.

item.title: Toyota RAV4 and Lexus NX may have loose brake bolts
item.description: On some 2024 RAV4 and 2025 Lexus NX vehicles, bolts holding the front brake caliper and the wheel hub bearing may not be tight enough. Loose bolts can rub against and damage the rubber hose that carries brake fluid to the caliper, or in the worst case let a wheel come off the vehicle. A leaking brake hose means weaker brakes and a longer distance to stop. A dealer will check and tighten the bolts and replace anything damaged, at no cost.

item.title: Toyota Corolla steering shaft can crack and break apart
item.description: The metal shaft that connects your steering wheel to the steering gear was made with cracks in it. Over time that shaft can break, and it may come apart from the steering column. If that happens while you are driving, the steering wheel stops turning the front wheels and you cannot steer the car. The cracks came from how the shaft was made at the factory. Your dealer will replace the whole shaft with a new one at no cost.

item.title: Toyota Tundra and Sequoia tires may lose air suddenly
item.description: The front and rear tires on the passenger side may have damage on the inner sidewall, which is the part of the tire facing under the vehicle where it is hard to see. Damage in that spot can let a tire lose its air all at once rather than going down slowly. A sudden flat while you are moving can pull the vehicle to one side and make it hard to control. A dealer will inspect the tires and replace any that are damaged.

item.title: Toyota Corolla Hybrid may lose brake power assist
item.description: These hybrids use a computer to help boost the force you put on the brake pedal. A software error in that computer can cut off the power assist while you are turning a corner. When the assist drops out, the brakes take much more effort and your car needs a longer distance to come to a stop, which makes a crash more likely. Toyota dealers will load corrected software into that brake control computer at no charge to you.

item.title: Toyota Sequoia Hybrid tow hitch cover can fall off
item.description: These SUVs have a small cover over the tow hitch opening in the rear bumper. On the affected vehicles that cover can work itself loose and fall off while you are driving. A piece of trim lying in a traffic lane is a hazard for the cars behind you, and someone could hit it or swerve to avoid it. The fix replaces the cover and changes the rear bumper so the new one stays put.

item.title: Gulf States Toyota vehicles have wrong weight capacity labels
item.description: These Toyotas were sold with accessories added through Gulf States Toyota. When accessories are added, a sticker is supposed to be placed on the vehicle showing how much less weight it can now carry in people and cargo. On these vehicles that sticker shows the wrong numbers. If you go by it, you could load the vehicle heavier than it is rated for. Gulf States Toyota is mailing corrected labels to owners at no charge; nothing on the vehicle needs repair.

item.title: Toyota Grand Highlander and Lexus TX curtain airbags deploy wrong
item.description: The side curtain airbags drop down from above the side windows in a crash and are meant to keep people from being thrown out of the vehicle. On these vehicles the airbag may not unroll the way it should, and if a window is open it can partly deploy outside the vehicle instead of covering the window opening. When that happens it does not protect the people sitting beside it as well as it is supposed to.

item.title: Toyota Highlander sold with tires rated too weak
item.description: These Highlanders were fitted with 20-inch add-on tires that are not rated to carry as much weight as the vehicle puts on them. Tires that are not strong enough for the load can be overloaded and fail while you are driving. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal rule on tire selection. Southeast Toyota will inspect the tires and the tire information sticker on the vehicle and replace them if needed, free of charge. Owner letters were mailed August 16, 2024.

item.title: Toyota Highlander Blackout Package tires rated too weak
item.description: These Highlanders were sold through Gulf States Toyota with a Blackout Package that adds 20-inch black wheels and tires. The tires that came on them are not rated to carry as much weight as the vehicle is allowed to carry. A tire asked to hold more weight than it was built for can fail. The dealer will check your tires, replace them if they are the wrong ones, and put on a new tire information sticker.

item.title: Toyota Tundra engine may fail and stall
item.description: Leftover debris from the factory may be inside the engine of these trucks and the Lexus LX600. That debris can damage the main bearings, the parts the crankshaft spins on, and if a bearing fails the engine can shut off while you are driving. You would lose engine power, possibly in traffic or at highway speed, which makes a crash more likely. Toyota dealers will replace the entire engine at no cost to you.
